author: NewsBreak
title: Justice Department Sues California Over Trans Student Title IX Violations in High School Sports - NewsBreak
text: SACRAMENTO — The Justice Department filed a lawsuit this week against the California Department of Education and the California Interscholastic Federation, accusing both of violating federal civil rights law by allowing male athletes to compete in girls’ high school sports. The lawsuit was announced in Washington and targets policies impacting schools and athletic programs across the state. According to the Justice Department, California’s current practices are depriving female student-athletes of fair and equal opportunities, a right protected under Title IX. The department’s complaint states that this is not only discriminatory but also unsafe. The lawsuit alleges that by permitting male students to compete in girls’ sports, the state has undermined decades of progress made under Title IX, which prohibits sex-based discrimination in education programs that receive federal funding. The California Department of Education oversees policies for local school districts, while the California Interscholastic Federation governs over 750,000 high school athletes in grades 9 through 12 across the state. The Justice Department noted that California received approximately $44.3 billion in federal education funds for the 2025 fiscal year, with around $3.8 billion still available for use. Attorney General Pamela Bondi emphasized the significance of the issue, stating, “The Governor of California has previously admitted that it is ‘deeply unfair’ to force women and girls to compete with men and boys in competitive sports. But not only is it ‘deeply unfair,’ it is also illegal under federal law. This Department of Justice will continue its fight to protect equal opportunities for women and girls in sports.” Harmeet K. Dhillon, Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Rights Division, added, “Title IX was enacted over half a century ago to protect women and girls from discrimination. The Justice Department will not stand for policies that deprive girls of their hard-earned athletic trophies and ignore their safety on the field and in private spaces. Young women should not have to sacrifice their rights to compete for scholarships, opportunities, and awards on the altar of woke gender ideology.” Bill Essayli, the United States Attorney for the Central District of California, said, “California is on the wrong side of the law and the wrong side of history. Women deserve dignity, respect, and an equal opportunity to compete on their own sports teams. The time for talk is over. California must comply with Title IX and end its civil rights violations against women. No person, no state, is above the law.”
